subject: Media Literacy
title: The History of Media Bias
description: Learn The History of Media Bias in one minute.

hook.text: In the 1800s, newspapers were openly partisan. The idea of 'unbiased news' is actually the historical exception.

buildup.text: Partisan press was the norm for centuries. Newspapers were funded by political parties and served their interests.

discovery.text: The objectivity standard emerged in the early 1900s when newspapers wanted to appeal to broader audiences for ad revenue.

twist.text: Objectivity wasn't born from principle. It was born from business — neutral papers attracted more advertisers.

climax.text: Today's media is returning to its partisan roots — not because of ideology, but because partisan content gets more clicks.

punchline.text: Objectivity was a business decision. So is the return to partisanship.

quiz.question: Why did the objectivity standard emerge in journalism?
options: Neutral papers attracted broader audiences and more advertisers
